value.kbd_note: X11 desktop (twm, focus follows the pointer); the xterm at the origin holds the keyboard once the daemon's first warp lands there. Type into the xterm.
value.note: no audio device; ABSOLUTE pointer via x11warp into the guest XFree86 server (loopback SLIRP forward 6076->6000), buttons + keys over D-Bus PS/2

labctl.notes: no exec channel: drive via QMP keys and read the framebuffer. Pointer MOTION is absolute through the guest X server (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11warp on SH_X11WARP_DISPLAY=127.0.0.1:76; the launcher publishes a loopback SLIRP forward 6076->10.0.2.15:6000 and the golden carries xhost +10.0.2.2). Buttons and keys ride the PS/2 path over D-Bus. SINGLE INJECTOR: nothing else may move this pointer. disk.qcow2 is the only block device and carries the golden vmstate under /opt/qemu-beos.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # netbsd14 (VMID 176) — NetBSD 1.4.1 i386 (1999), XFree86 3.3.3.1 on Cirrus; absolute pointer via x11warp.

launcherParity.reason: pc-i440fx-11.0 under KVM with -vga cirrus (XFree86 3.3 SVGA cirrus driver), one IDE disk carrying the golden vmstate, ne2k_pci on SLIRP (restrict=on) with the loopback X forward 6076->6000 for x11warp, plus a second ne2k_pci on the retronet tap netbsd14rn0 (vmbr-rn); no audio device

qemuBuild.base: QEMU 11.0.2 (the same version as the host pve-qemu-kvm 11.0.2-1, so machine type pc-i440fx-11.0 is unchanged)
qemuBuild.note: Same installed build as beos (/opt/qemu-beos); see beos.json for provenance.

museum.periodBrowser: Lynx 2.8.2rel.1 (built from source on the guest; NetBSD 1.4.1 ships no browser in base)
museum.blurb: NetBSD 1.4.1, August 1999: the portable BSD that ran one source tree on every architecture it touched, with sysinst, the new UVM memory system and pkgsrc — here on i386 under the last monolithic XFree86 3.3 server, a year before the 4.0 rewrite.
museum.notes: Live streamhost station. Boots to an XFree86 3.3.3.1 twm session on the Cirrus adapter with an xterm, xclock and xcalc; the pointer is absolute because the daemon warps the guest X server itself (x11warp over a loopback SLIRP forward) while clicks and keys ride the PS/2 path. Since 2026-09-03 it is also on the retronet: a second ne2k_pci on the tap netbsd14rn0 carries the web and ICQ planes, so the ready scene shows mICQ 0.4.12 signed in as UIN 17600 with HiveBot on the contact list and Lynx 2.8.2 on http://search.retronet/. disk.qcow2 is the single block device and carries the golden vmstate.

reset.fixture: NetBSD 1.4.1 twm desktop (XFree86 3.3.3.1 SVGA on the Cirrus GD5446, 1024x768x8, custom KHMIN kernel): xterm 'NetBSD 1.4.1' 80x28 at the origin holding a root shell, Calculator at (640,80), xclock top-right, and the two retronet windows on the bottom row — 'ICQ - mICQ' 80x20 at (0,430) showing mICQ 0.4.12 signed in as UIN 17600 with HiveBot online in the contact list, and 'Web Browser - Lynx' 80x20 at (510,430) rendering http://search.retronet/. The golden carries xhost +10.0.2.2 so the x11warp pointer works on every restore (proven 2026-09-03: scene 5.9 s after launch+cont, X handshake 1.0 s; mICQ signs back on unattended ~45 s after a restore whose OSCAR session the gateway had already reaped).
